name: AI Grant Consultant
operator: Granter (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Granter's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Chat-based agent, onboarded with the organisation's details and past applications, that matches funding calls, checks eligibility and admissibility, drafts applications section by section with playbooks, scores drafts with an Evaluator, and supports post-approval reporting. The user submits the application.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: The note says Super Bock prepared a submitted application with the agent. The name Super Bock appears in none of the four sources of the scan (searched the fidelidade, marinha, blog and privacy texts). Remove that sentence. The Fidelidade page does say 'the two agents are live, and the platform is actively being used to identify new opportunities and begin drafting applications', and it names a customer, so the badge claim rests on a named customer in a pilot in its 'initial phase of a planned 12-month cycle', with no sessions, tasks or pull request counts. The span is present and under fifteen words. Note that the pilot is described as at its initial phase and results are due at the 6-month mark.

The marinha page has the stat labels '200' with 'Relevant funding opportunities added to a defence grants database' and '2w -> 2h' with 'first drafts presenting significant time saving'. The note's figures are on the page, but the span only supports the 200 figure, not the two weeks to two hours claim. The page figures are stated by the vendor in a case study, with no method or baseline given. 'Its value is measured' is a stretch for a count of database entries and an unexplained before/after label; consider quoting the 2w to 2h label as a second span or lowering to a note that no measurement method is stated. The grade 'documented' is acceptable only as 'the page reports figures', not as a measurement.

The span is present in the privacy policy: 'the platform does not take decisions about you on its own.' But the sentence is a data-protection statement about decisions concerning a person (the data subject), under a 'How we use AI' heading, not a limit on what the agent may do. The indicator is 'A limit on it is a rule in prose'. The credit is to a nearby fact. This answer is one of two that give Control level 1 (the other is I38), so it should not be counted unless the assessor argues it states a limit on the agent.

Span 'Users review and approve them before any submission or decision' is in the privacy policy, and it supports approval before submission. The note's second clause, 'the submission itself is made by the user', is not on the privacy policy page cited as source. It is on the blog page FAQ: 'Does Granter submit the application for me? No. The final submission is done by you'. Cite the blog as a second source or drop the clause. Credit to I38 is reasonable: a submission to a funder is the high-impact action. Control level 1 holds on this answer alone.

The span is on the fidelidade page ('trained using detailed information about Fidelidade's business and past applications', apostrophe aside). It supports 'AI platform with the organisation's own data'. Nothing in any source says it runs without executing arbitrary code, which is the second half of the indicator. Also the Fidelidade case describes a tailored pilot, not necessarily the default product; mode 'default' is doubtful. I02 is the second leg of the I07 route to Autonomy 2, but I16 alone gives level 2, so the level does not change.

Span present in the privacy policy, the policy says 'outputs are suggestions' and users review and approve before any submission or decision. The indicator says the person approves each action; the page says before submission or decision, not each step. Acceptable as stated; the card level A2 rests on this answer alone, so it is the one to keep sharp. I07 uses the identical span and is the same fact; fine, but it is not independent evidence.

Span 'Granter is being evaluated by three different Navy units' is in the marinha page, in the sentence 'The partnership is currently in the certification phase for the Navy Tested programme'. The note says 'a certification process run by the Navy'; the page names the programme but does not say who runs it, so say 'a certification phase for the Navy Tested programme'. Certification is in progress, not granted. Tier is declared: this is the vendor's own account of the Navy's evaluation, not a Navy publication. Grade 'documented' is fine for that.

Quote is on the blog page, attributed to Bernardo Tavares, CTO at Granter; the note's 'the CTO' is correct. The span and the extraction from official documents clause are both in the quote. Pass, with the note that it is a vendor spokesperson's statement.

Checked against the pages. I07: privacy policy says 'outputs are suggestions' and users review and approve. I09: the blog says the consultant scans 'regional, national and EU opportunities' and the span covers public and private funding; domain is grants. I20: privacy policy opening says the platform helps organisations find, prepare and manage applications for grants and other funding. I56: 'AI-generated content is presented as such inside the platform.' Spans found, under fifteen words, grades documented, mode default (stated generally, no opt-in found).

The 'announced' field cites granter.ai/about and the home page, which are not sources of the scan; the card does not rely on them. The blog page still carries 'Automated Submission (coming soon)' text while the FAQ says the user submits; the scan handles this correctly by not crediting submission automation. No I08/I17 answer, so no level three; none of the checked evidence is an adjective.

Card A2 R1 C1 O1. No level 3 or 4. A2 rests on I16 (suggest, person approves). R1 on I09. C1 on I47 and I38; if I47 is removed, I38 alone still gives C1. O1 on I20 plus I56 and I58 (I20 and I56 from the privacy policy, I58 from the blog). The levels are consistent with the evidence once the I47 weakness is noted; they do not change if the should-fix items are applied.

Scope of the source. The privacy policy (page dated 'Last updated: Nov 9, 2026', the day before the scan) never names the AI Grant Consultant or any agent: it speaks of 'the Granter platform' and 'AI models'. Three answers (I16, I07, I38) cite the one sentence 'Users review and approve them before any submission or decision' (ten words, exact, found on the page). The scan's subject is the AI Grant Consultant; the card's A2 and C1 rest on a company-wide data-protection page, not on a page about the agent. The indicator I16 says the person approves each action; the policy says before any submission or decision, which is coarser. The blog FAQ on the cited agent page says 'The final submission is done by you on the relevant platform', which is the agent-specific, stronger source for I38 and I16 and is not cited in either answer. Cite the blog as the source (or as a second source) for I38 and state in the note that the policy is platform-wide, or lower the answers. I07 and I16 are one fact counted twice; the card shows I07 as used for A2, which suggests independent support it does not have.

Openness level 1 depends on I20 alone (I56 or I58 can supply the other half, but nothing replaces I20). I20 asks that the purpose and permitted tasks are stated in writing. The span is the 'Who we are' line of the privacy policy: 'helps organisations find, prepare and manage applications for grants and other funding'. It is a one-line description of the company platform, in a legal page, with no permitted tasks and no mention of the agent. The AI Grant Consultant's own purpose is stated on the blog page, which would be the better source. Re-point I20 to the blog page or state in the note that only a purpose, not permitted tasks, is given.

Span 'AI-generated content is presented as such inside the platform.' is exact and on the policy page. The indicator is that the agent tells the people it talks to that it is an AI; the policy sentence labels generated content in the platform, a related but different fact. Not decisive, since I58 also supplies the second half of O1, but the note should say 'labels AI-generated content' (it does) and not be read as disclosure in conversation.

Span 'collect all important information, like previous applications, institutional data' is exact (ten words) and in a quote from the CTO on the blog page, who is named there. The quote says 'We onboard the company and collect' the information, which describes Granter's onboarding step, not data the agent reads at run time; the note says 'the data the agent uses', a small stretch. Keep, mark as the vendor's statement.

Verified against the Fidelidade page: the span 'the platform is actively being used to identify new opportunities and begin drafting applications' is exact (fourteen words), and the page title names the AI Grant Consultant, so the product link is sound. The note matches the page (initial phase of a planned 12-month cycle, two agents live, preliminary results at the 6-month mark). Weak points to keep visible: a single named customer, a pilot, no usage counts, and the badge is the customer's pilot described by the vendor. The Super Bock case study (granter.ai/case-studies/superbock, which loads and names the AI Grant Consultant) is the better second source and could be added to the scan's sources and captured instead of being listed only under not_credited.

Studio response is true: the span 'The pilot has already delivered measurable results:' is on the Navy page, seven words, and the note names both figures (+200 opportunities added to a defence grants database; '2w -> 2h' with first drafts) and says no method or baseline is stated. The note's phrase 'from two weeks to two hours' reads the page's '2w' and '2h' labels; reasonable but an interpretation. The page heading is 'Early Results', which the note could use. Q21 is outside the public levels; no card effect. Answered.

Studio response is true: the note now says 'a certification phase for the Navy Tested programme', that certification is not granted, and the span is exact on the Navy page. Remaining nuance: the page also says the Navy 'initiated a formal certification process', so the declared tier is right. Answered.

The not_credited entry for Super Bock names a URL that is not a source of the scan and a name that is in none of the four captured pages; the rule allows names from a source listed there, and the listed page does exist and carries the name, so this is within the rule. The I47 entry quotes the blog FAQ ('access to submission-platform accounts is restricted for Granter'), which is on the page. The announced items cite granter.ai and granter.ai/about: I fetched both; the home page has '2x' higher approval rates and '75%' less time, and the About page has the 'Future' entry 'Smarter AI, deeper integrations', so those are supported, though neither page is captured in the scan's vault.

Card A2 R1 C1 O1; there is no level three or four, so I argued against the weakest credited levels. A2 rests on I16 alone (I07 has no second leg after I02 was removed): a platform-wide policy sentence about review before submission or decision, in prose, not an artefact; if I16 is removed Autonomy drops to none from this scan (I15 is not answered), which breaks the rule of no card below level one in every dimension. C1 rests on I38 alone, the same sentence, so one sentence in one page supports A2 and C1 and, through I07, the 'used' list for A. O1 rests on I20 (a one-line company description) plus I56 or I58; remove I20 and O1 falls. R1 rests on I09, a blog FAQ line on coverage; reach as 'works inside its own product' is not tested by a coverage statement. All modes are default and honest, no adjectives found. The levels are defensible as level one and two claims but each rests on a thin, partly out-of-scope source; strengthening them needs the blog FAQ for I38 and I16 and the blog purpose text for I20.

Verified by fetching the four pages myself: every span is present verbatim and under fifteen words; the S1 Super Bock sentence is gone; I47 and I02 are removed and explained in not_credited with text that matches the pages; the I38 note no longer carries the blog clause; I52 wording matches the Navy page; the I67 span now covers both figures. Round-one findings fully answered: S1, I67, I47, I02, I52, I16, I58, I07/I09/I20/I56 group, announced, levels note. I38 is answered in the sense asked (second clause dropped) but see the scope finding above.

not_credited.what: I47 (a limit on it is a rule in prose)
not_credited.why: The privacy policy sentence 'the platform does not take decisions about you on its own' is a data-protection statement about decisions concerning the data subject, not a limit on what the agent may do. The blog FAQ line 'access to submission-platform accounts is restricted for Granter' is an access restriction, not a prose rule of the expectation kind; neither is credited.

not_credited.what: I02 (own data, without executing arbitrary code)
not_credited.why: The Fidelidade page says a tailored pilot's agents were trained on the customer's business and past applications; no source says the agent runs without executing arbitrary code, and the pilot is not shown to be the default product.

not_credited.what: Super Bock as a customer for the In production badge
not_credited.why: Not in the scan's sources; the Fidelidade pilot alone carries S1.
